memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If anyone gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep or any other animal to their neighbor for safekeeping and it dies or is injured or is taken away while no one is looking, the issue between them will be settled by the taking of an oath before the Lord that the neighbor did not lay hands on the other person's property. The owner is to accept this, and no restitution is required." - Exodus 22:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Sometimes there are no witnesses. An animal entrusted to a neighbour dies or wanders off, and no one saw what happened. How can the truth be settled? God's answer is striking: the keeper swears an oath before the Lord himself. When human eyes cannot see, the matter is placed directly into God's hands, and His name settles it. The owner must accept it, trusting that God will deal with any lie.

This reveals a God who is deeply woven into everyday honesty. An oath "before the Lord" meant that God was the true witness, the one no deception could escape. People could act faithfully even when no human could verify it, because they knew Someone always could. Honesty was not merely about avoiding getting caught; it was about living before the face of God.

We are called to that same integrity. In a world where people often behave well only when watched, followers of Christ are invited to live consistently before an audience of One. God sees the private email, the quiet choice, the unwitnessed moment. Far from being a threat, this is a comfort: your unseen faithfulness is never truly unseen. God notices, God remembers, and God honours the heart that keeps faith when no one else is looking.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I live with integrity even when no human being would ever know?
How does knowing God always sees change the way I make private choices?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are the witness to every hidden moment of my life. Give me a heart of true integrity, faithful before You even when no one else can see. Amen.
